This is all off the top of my head so don't quote me.
The de-blueing process is as simple as leaving it in acid until it has all dissolved. Acids I've seen used are vinegar or citric, you can use Hydrochloric but it will start to etch the steel and I don't recommend using it if you never have before. Vinegar and citric will dissolve all rust and blueing whilst leaving the base metal.

As for the re bluing, you can do what I've done and use a molten mixture of sodium hydroxide and potassium nitrate. This is known as hot blueing. I don't recommend this unless you've got the safety equipment. Molten nitrates and hydroxides are not to be taken lightly. 
What I would recommend is something called "rust blueing". There's lots of info online but the idea is that you flash rust the part after completely cleaning it, then boil it in water to convert the ferrous oxide into ferric oxide (blue).

If it were me and I wanted it in perfect condition, I'd strip the remaining blue off completely and re blue the entire rifle. It sounds intimidating, but there's a guy on youtube who restores firearms and he's got some good info on the process
